lesson.title: Identify datasets and document their origins
lesson.summary: Identify dataset purposes, origins and preparation decisions.

prerequisites.reason: Dataset use depends on what the system is intended to do.

blocks: A **training dataset** is used to fit a model. A **validation dataset** helps evaluate and choose or tune development choices. A **testing dataset** assesses performance against the chosen criteria.

Where model training uses data, Article 10’s quality criteria apply whenever the relevant sets are used. For high-risk systems not using model-training techniques, paragraphs 2–4 and Article 4a(1) apply only to testing sets. Do not demand a fictional training set where no training occurs.

**Dataset provenance** records collection processes and origin. For personal data, include the original collection purpose. Northbridge receiving old applicant records does not by itself establish permission for every new use.

Data governance also records design choices, assumptions about what the data measures or represents, and availability, quantity and suitability of needed sets. A purchase receipt is not a complete provenance record.
**Data preparation** includes annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment and aggregation. Annotation adds descriptive information; labelling assigns the target or category used for a task.

A label “successful applicant” may reflect past hiring preferences rather than future job competence. Record the assumption before treating it as a suitable target. Document relevant preparation operations so the result can be explained.

Case: Northbridge has applicant records, unknown original purpose, undocumented cleaning and labels based only on past selection. Ask for evidence of origins, permissions, preparation and what the target represents.
Keeping dataset roles distinct helps inspect which evidence supports which development choice. A large folder called “training” does not establish appropriate governance.
